bihar_raw_news.title: NHAI Allocates ₹50 Crore For Wildlife Conservation Along Varanasi-Kolkata Expressway
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / India / Trending / NHAI Allocates ₹50 Crore For Wildlife Conservation Along Varanasi-Kolkata Expressway NHAI has rolled out a wildlife conservation and environmental protection plan along the Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Expressway in Bihar. by Tanvi Shrivastava Updated: October 18, 2026 12:04 PM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Wikimedia Commons The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has allocated around ₹50 crore to Bihar’s Environment, Forest and Climate Change Department to implement an environmental conservation and wildlife mitigation plan along the Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Expressway. The plan aims to protect wildlife habitats, conserve endangered species and improve road safety while supporting connectivity to key religious and tourist destinations, including Bodh Gaya in Gaya district and the Sun Temple at Deo in neighbouring Aurangabad district. Scroll down to know more. NHAI Provides 50 Crore For Wildlife Range Along Varanasi-Kolkata Expressway According to Times of India, the plan covers wildlife habitat improvement, the conservation of selected Schedule I species, soil and water conservation, forest fire management, and monitoring and evaluation. The initiative also includes planting around 45,000 saplings along the expressway corridor. NHAI’s regional office in Patna organised a media tour on Friday to showcase the project’s progress, engineering features and regional significance. Project director Devendra Kumar Bansal told the portal that the 33-km Package VII, being constructed in Bihar’s Gaya district at a cost of ₹1,248 crore, has achieved around 36% physical progress. The stretch runs from Anarban Saleya village to Sangrampur, covering the section between kilometre 151 and kilometre 184. The package is being developed under the Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM). The wildlife conservation plan has been prepared in coordination with the state forest department and the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI). The package includes two elephant underpasses and two animal overpasses to allow wildlife to cross the expressway safely. These structures, along with other mitigation measures, are designed to reduce disruptions to animal movement and improve road safety. Also Read: Video: Mysore Palace Sees Tourist Jam In Long Weekend; Netizens: & Some Still Stuck On Highway& Expressway To Feature Cameras And Trauma Centres To Boost Road Safety The expressway will also feature high-quality cameras installed at one-kilometre intervals to support monitoring and safety. Trauma centres are planned every 30 km to provide timely medical assistance to passengers in case of emergencies. The Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Expressway will begin at Rivasa in Uttar Pradesh’s Varanasi district and pass through Chandauli in Uttar Pradesh before entering Bihar. It will traverse Kaimur, Rohtas, Aurangabad and Gaya districts, followed by several districts in Jharkhand, including Chatra, Hazaribag, Ranchi, Bokaro, Dhanbad and Ramgarh. Also Read: How India Is Using AI To Find Accident-Prone Highway Stretches Before They Turn Deadly The route will then pass through Purulia and Bankura in West Bengal before connecting to Kolkata. Along with improving regional connectivity, the project is intended to provide better access to important religious and tourist destinations while incorporating measures to protect wildlife and the environment. Jocelyn Fernandes Published 18 Oct 2026, 07:55 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Assam, Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Sikkim, West Bengal and more — Today we take a look at the full list of states that have announced DA and DR hikes this year. ( AI generated image for representational purposes only ) AI Quick Read In line with the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) recommendations, the government hikes dearness allowance (DA) biannually using data from the All-India Consumer Price Index ( AICPI ). Over 1 crore beneficiaries, comprising about 50 lakh central government employees and nearly 65 lakh pensioners, including defence and railway personnel and retirees, gain from DA and Dearness Relief (DR) hikes. DA is a percentage of employees ' basic pay that aims to mitigate the impact of the rising cost of living and inflation. Notably, announcements from the Centre come in March and October, with rollouts in January and July. The last hike was announced in April this year, when the Finance Ministry increased DA from 58% to 60% of basic salary, effective from 1 January 2026. Meanwhile, DA revision is also under discussion by the 8th CPC , which is expected to submit its final recommendations around 18 months after its constitution, by May 2027 at the latest. It hiked basic salaries between ₹ 48,000 and ₹ 1,17,000 and DA from ₹ 435 to ₹ 1,050. Later, the Indian Railways also announced a 2% hike in DA and DR for staff and pensioners. Here's a look at the full list of DA hikes announced by states so far: Kerala hiked DA and dearness relief (DR) by two percentage points, from 35% to 37%, be paid with the October 2026 salary, disbursed in November. The hike primarily covers state government employees, teachers, full-time contingent employees and local government staff. It also includes state service pensioners, family pensioners, and eligible ex-gratia pensioners and their families. This follows an earlier increase in DA and DR from 25% to 35% in February 2026. bihar_raw_news.content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): Haryana, Delhi and Bihar have agreed to 1,200 MW solar and battery storage projects with Madhya Pradesh. Approval for these projects is pending at the state government level. Once approved and operational, the projects will provide Madhya Pradesh with additional electricity during evening hours, when power demand is at its peak. Sources in the new and renewable energy department said the proposed projects include 500 MW each in partnership with Delhi and Haryana and 200 MW with Bihar. As far as projects with Haryana, Delhi and Bihar are concerned, the generated power will be used by the partner states on a rotational basis. Madhya Pradesh will draw power from October till April, the period during which power demand remains higher. On the other hand, Haryana, Delhi and Bihar would draw power from April till September. Apart from this, Mandsaur's pumped storage project is nearing completion. Its capacity is 1,920 MW. At least 10 more similar projects are in the pipeline in different parts of the state. Projects can be set up in one or two years Additional Chief Secretary for the New and Renewable Energy Department Manu Shrivastava said, We can set up projects within one or two years and supply inexpensive power once the energy department is willing to purchase it. Solar power cheaper than thermal energy The power produced by solar projects is far cheaper than the energy produced by thermal projects. The solar energy rate is Rs 2.15 per unit in comparison to Rs 6 per unit of thermal energy. The installation period for a thermal power plant is at least six years, while solar projects hardly need 12-18 months for their installation. This means that through solar power projects, power generation starts much earlier in comparison to thermal power projects. national_raw_news.content: In West Bengal, 19 people lost their lives and 25 others were injured in a stampede at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata last evening. The incident occurred at around 8 PM, during the Maha Saptami celebrations. According to media reports, heavy rain and a sudden rush of visitors led to chaos at the crowded pandal. Several people reportedly fell amid the rush, triggering a stampede-like situation. The injured were rushed to Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, R-G Kar Medical College and Hospital, and N-R-S Medical College and Hospital for treatment. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, the state Health Minister and senior government officials visited the hospitals to assess the situation and review the treatment being provided to the injured. The Chief Minister also announced compensation of 25 lakh rupees and a Group D government job for the family of each deceased person. Later, speaking to reporters, the Chief Minister said police have detained the Durga Puja organisers, private security guards and staff on duty for questioning. Describing the incident as tragic, Mr Adhikari said the administration’s immediate priority was to ensure proper medical treatment for the injured. He said, preliminary reports suggest that an announcement made over the loudspeaker by the puja organisers triggered a sudden rush among visitors, leading to the stampede. The Chief Minister announced that a Special Investigation Team, or SIT, headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta High Court, will investigate the stampede at the Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata. The SIT will include members of the Special Task Force, the Criminal Investigation Department and other government departments. Meanwhile, the Anti-Rowdy Section of Kolkata Police has collected CCTV footage from the site of the incident. The Chief Minister said the footage would be examined and strict action would be taken against anyone found responsible for failing to manage the crowd. Mr. Adhikari asserted that no one responsible for the lapses would be spared. The Chorbagan community puja pandal has been closed, and the site has been handed over to forensic experts, the police Special Task Force and the Fire Brigade for investigation. The Chorbagan Durga Puja, which has grown in popularity in recent years, attracts large crowds. Meanwhile, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who is currently in Kolkata, is monitoring the situation and is in constant touch with the Chief Minister and other senior state officials. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said, all official programmes, including those involving the Union Home Minister, have been postponed in view of the tragedy. Mr Shah was scheduled to visit several Durga Puja pandals today. Union Home Minister said, he will visit the injured in the hospital today. The Chief Minister urged Durga Puja organisers, particularly those hosting elaborate theme-based celebrations, to ensure adequate lighting and sufficient entry and exit points to prevent overcrowding and ensure public safety. He stressed that human lives must take precedence over decorative themes, as organisers across Kolkata and other parts of West Bengal compete to create increasingly elaborate and attractive pandals.
